paragraphs: Alanis Morissette is a Canadian-American singer-songwriter often called the “Queen of Alt-Rock Angst.” Jagged Little Pill made her a defining voice of 1990s rock; she has sold more than 60 million records worldwide.
Her honors include seven Grammy Awards, a Brit Award, fourteen Juno Awards, nominations for Golden Globe and Tony Awards, and induction into Canada’s Walk of Fame.

The Weeknd (Abel Tesfaye) is a Canadian singer-songwriter whose alternative R&B and pop catalog made him one of the defining pop figures of the 2010s and 2020s. He is known for a light tenor and falsetto, dark cinematic videos, and stadium-scale touring.
His accolades include four Grammy Awards, 20 Billboard Music Awards, 22 Juno Awards, six American Music Awards, a Super Bowl LV halftime show, and a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

Adam Lambert became a global name as runner-up on American Idol in 2009, then launched a solo career that mixed theatrical rock with pop. Early albums such as For Your Entertainment established him as a charting recording artist.
He has since toured the world as the vocalist for Queen + Adam Lambert, one of the most successful live rock partnerships of the last decade.

Usher is a defining figure in contemporary R&B and pop — ranked among Rolling Stone’s greatest singers and Billboard’s greatest pop stars of the 21st century. Breakthrough albums from My Way through Confessions produced a run of US number-one singles.
He has sold tens of millions of records, collected multiple Grammy Awards, and headlined Super Bowl LVIII in 2024.
Carrie Underwood won American Idol in 2005 and became one of the central country artists of the 21st century, credited with keeping female country voices at the center of mainstream radio.
She has earned eight Grammy Awards, sold tens of millions of records, and is a member of the Grand Ole Opry.

Stone Temple Pilots emerged from San Diego as one of the biggest American rock bands of the 1990s. Core and Purple helped define post-grunge radio, with Scott Weiland’s original run as frontman still the catalog most audiences know.
The band won the Grammy Award for Best Hard Rock Performance for “Plush” and remains a staple of rock radio and touring.
Scott Weiland was the voice of Stone Temple Pilots and later of the hard-rock supergroup Velvet Revolver. Across both bands he became one of the most recognizable rock singers of the 1990s and 2000s.
He won Grammy Awards with STP and with Velvet Revolver, and also recorded as a solo artist and with Art of Anarchy.
Shakira, the Colombian singer-songwriter dubbed the “Queen of Latin Music,” helped take Spanish-language pop worldwide and is credited with a major role in popularizing Hispanophone music globally.
She has won Grammy and Latin Grammy Awards, performed official FIFA World Cup anthems, and sold tens of millions of records across Spanish and English catalogs.
Sugar Ray formed in Newport Beach, California, and shifted from early nu-metal into radio-ready pop-rock after the 1997 hit “Fly.” Fronted by Mark McGrath, the band became a late-1990s MTV staple.
Follow-up singles kept them on US and international charts and made summer-radio pop-rock one of the era’s most familiar sounds.
Neil Young is one of the most influential singer-songwriters in rock — from Buffalo Springfield and Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young to a vast solo catalog often backed by Crazy Horse.
He is a two-time Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductee, an Officer of the Order of Canada, and a reference point for folk, country-rock, and the sound that later fed grunge.
Operator was the Los Angeles post-grunge project of actor-musician Johnny Strong, known on screen from films such as Black Hawk Down and The Fast and the Furious.
Mid-2000s releases including “Can You Feel It Now?” placed the band on US rock radio alongside Strong’s film career.
Velvet Revolver brought together Guns N’ Roses alumni Slash, Duff McKagan, and Matt Sorum with Scott Weiland and guitarist Dave Kushner. The hard-rock supergroup was active from 2002 until 2008.
Debut album Contraband topped the Billboard 200, and “Slither” won the Grammy Award for Best Hard Rock Performance.

Guns N’ Roses formed in Los Angeles in 1985 and turned Appetite for Destruction into one of the best-selling debut albums of all time, with “Welcome to the Jungle,” “Paradise City,” and “Sweet Child o’ Mine” still among rock’s most played songs.
The band has sold more than 100 million records worldwide and was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2012.

Maroon 5 grew from the Los Angeles band Kara’s Flowers into one of the most successful pop-rock acts of the 2000s. Songs About Jane launched worldwide hits such as “This Love” and “She Will Be Loved.”
Later singles including “Moves Like Jagger” added further chart dominance, Grammy Awards, and stadium-scale touring.

The Red Hot Chili Peppers have fused funk, punk, and alternative rock since 1982. With more than 120 million records sold, they are among the best-selling bands of all time and a constant presence on alternative radio.
They hold multiple Billboard Alternative chart records, have won several Grammy Awards, and entered the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2012.
Dave Grohl formed Foo Fighters after Nirvana, turning a solo project into one of the most awarded rock bands of the last 30 years. The group grew from the 1995 debut album into a global stadium act.
Foo Fighters have won 15 Grammy Awards and were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2021.

Mariah Carey — dubbed the “Songbird Supreme” — is known for a five-octave range, whistle register, and a record 19 Billboard Hot 100 number-one singles. Rolling Stone ranked her among the greatest singers of all time in 2023.
She has sold more than 200 million records worldwide and won multiple Grammy Awards, with a catalog that runs from Vision of Love through holiday standard “All I Want for Christmas Is You.”
The Harlem Gospel Singers were founded in 1991 by soul and gospel singer Queen Esther Marrow, mixing gospel with jazz, pop, and R&B for audiences far beyond the church.

The company toured concert halls and churches worldwide, including appearances at the Vatican and the White House, becoming one of the best-known international gospel touring productions of the 1990s and 2000s.
Puddle of Mudd formed in Kansas City and broke through with Come Clean (2001). The single “Blurry” reached the Billboard Hot 100 top five and remains the band’s signature song.
Come Clean sold more than five million copies, making them one of the defining post-grunge acts of the early 2000s.

R.E.M. helped define American alternative rock from Athens, Georgia, from 1980 until they retired in 2011. Michael Stipe’s voice and Peter Buck’s jangle guitar became a template for the college-rock generation that followed.
The band sold more than 85 million albums, won multiple Grammy Awards, and was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2007.
Ute Lemper is a German singer and actress whose career spans chanson, musical theatre, and the concert stage — including work with orchestras such as the Tapiola Sinfonietta.
She won the Molière Award as Sally Bowles in the original Paris Cabaret and the Olivier Award for Best Actress in a Musical as Velma Kelly in Chicago.
Zwan was Billy Corgan’s post–Smashing Pumpkins alternative-rock group with Jimmy Chamberlin, Paz Lenchantin, David Pajo, and Matt Sweeney.
Their only album, Mary Star of the Sea (2003), reached the US top ten before the band split the same year during the supporting tour.

Dream Theater is a leading progressive metal band, formed in Boston in 1985 and known for virtuoso playing and long-form compositions. The classic touring lineup has centered on John Petrucci, John Myung, James LaBrie, Jordan Rudess, and Mike Portnoy.
The group has won Grammy Awards for its later work and built a global touring audience across four decades.

The Golden Gospel Singers were founded in 1991 by Harlem-born producer and choir director Bob Singleton. The company assembled American gospel vocalists for annual European seasons of more than 100 concerts, becoming a familiar name on church and theatre bills in Germany and neighboring countries.
Their 1998 album Beyond Y2K was released through Koch/Universal in Germany during that touring era. Andy mixed FOH on the 1997–2000 European gospel run, including church acoustics with limited PA.

Glenn Hughes is the English singer and bassist known for Trapeze, Deep Purple’s Mk III and Mk IV years, and a brief tenure fronting Black Sabbath. He is renowned for funk-inspired bass playing and a wide, soulful vocal range.
He was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame as a member of Deep Purple.

The Michael Schenker Group is the hard-rock vehicle of German guitarist Michael Schenker, formerly of UFO and the Scorpions. Formed in London in 1979, MSG became a staple of European and Japanese hard rock.
A run of early-1980s studio and live albums — including Rock Will Never Die — established Schenker as one of the era’s defining lead guitarists.

Modern Talking — Dieter Bohlen and Thomas Anders — is often cited as Germany’s most successful pop duo. Hits such as “You’re My Heart, You’re My Soul,” “You Can Win If You Want,” and “Cheri, Cheri Lady” topped charts across Europe in the mid-1980s.
The catalog remains a fixture of German pop history, with later reunions returning the duo to European stages.

MOMIX is the Connecticut-based dance company founded by choreographer Moses Pendleton, an offshoot of Pilobolus known for illusionistic, athletic stage works that have toured internationally since the 1980s — including a solo created for the 1980 Winter Olympics.
Tarkan, the German-born Turkish pop star, broke worldwide with “Şımarık” in 1997 and followed it with European hits including “Şıkıdım” and “Bounce,” becoming one of Turkey’s best-known pop exports.

Al Bano (Albano Carrisi) is an Italian singer and actor whose career spans seven decades and more than 25 million records sold. He is known for a wide vocal range and a long presence in European popular music.
He became internationally famous with Romina Power; the duo’s Sanremo-era hits made Al Bano & Romina Power a fixture of European pop and television.
Quannum World was a 2004 United States club and touring act. The dates sit in Andy’s monitor credits from a year that also included Maroon 5, the Red Hot Chili Peppers, and other arena-scale work.

Alice in Chains is one of the defining Seattle bands of the late 1980s and 1990s, alongside Nirvana, Pearl Jam, and Soundgarden. Their dark, harmony-heavy sound sat at the crossroads of grunge, metal, and alternative rock.

The catalog around Facelift, Dirt, and Jar of Flies earned multiple Grammy nominations and a lasting place on heavy-rock and alternative radio. The band later returned to the stage with William DuVall joining Jerry Cantrell.
Sebastian Bach rose to fame as the frontman of Skid Row, whose late-1980s albums made the Canadian singer a global hard-rock voice with hits such as “18 and Life” and “I Remember You.”
After leaving the band in 1996 he continued as a solo artist and on stage, including Broadway and television appearances.

Enrique Iglesias is a Spanish singer who became one of the best-selling Latin artists of the 1990s before crossing into English-language pop. Early Spanish albums on Fonovisa made him the decade’s leading Spanish-language act.
He has collected a long run of Billboard Latin number-ones, worldwide pop hits, and major Latin music awards spanning both languages.

Black Rebel Motorcycle Club formed in San Francisco in 1998, taking their name from The Wild One. The group’s garage, blues, and shoegaze-leaning rock built a dedicated international following from the debut B.R.M.C. onward.
Albums such as Howl widened the sound beyond the early Jesus and Mary Chain comparisons and kept the band on festival and theatre stages worldwide.
Local Natives is a Los Angeles indie-rock band that broke out with Gorilla Manor (2009) and a much-praised live reputation built on stacked harmonies and percussion.
Festival stages and later albums established them as a staple of 2010s American indie, with a catalog that moved from Silver Lake rooms to international touring.

Travis Scott is a Houston rapper, singer, and producer with five Billboard Hot 100 number-one hits and more than a hundred charting songs. Astroworld-era touring made him one of the defining stadium hip-hop artists of the 2010s.
He has received numerous Grammy Award nominations, a Latin Grammy Award, and built the Cactus Jack imprint into a major hip-hop brand.
